title: R. K. Narayan's birth chart
metaDescription: R. K. Narayan's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 16.0° Libra. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 11.8° Cancer, in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 16.0° Libra: the second decan, whose classical sub-ruler is Saturn. An air sign, read here in its second face.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 27.3° Libra, Venus was at 0.7° Sagittarius, Mars was at 17.5° Virgo. Read together: a mind at home in argument and pattern; taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Jupiter trine Saturn, 1.2° of separation. Trines are read as inheritance rather than achievement: the ease is genuine, and nothing about it was earned. Behind it, Jupiter conjunction Neptune at 2.2°, and the Sun square Neptune at 3.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Venus stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has three entries for this chart. The Sun in Libra at 16.0° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; the Moon in Cancer at 11.8° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Cancer at 10.4° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: water 4, air 3, earth 2, fire 1 across the elements, and cardinal 6, mutable 4 across the modalities. A water emphasis reads as porousness: the room is registered whole, long before it is analysed in parts. Saturn and Pluto were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Cancer for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.0° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 11.8°.
